fullPassage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to ①<u>celebrate</u> every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be ②<u>protecting</u> because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and ③<u>humans</u>. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, ④<u>covering</u> an area as big as 210 soccer fields.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②protecting → protected: 'must be protected'에서 수동태(be + p.p.)가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② protecting → protected: 'must be + p.p.' 수동태 구문. 생태계가 보호'받는' 것.
❌ ① celebrate: 'enough to celebrate'에서 to부정사 적절.
❌ ③ humans: 'the environment and humans' 명사 병렬 적절.
❌ ④ covering: 분사구문으로 부가 설명. 적절.
det.tip: must be + p.p.(수동태): must be protected(보호되어야 한다). 조동사 + be + p.p.

questions.passage: The Camargue is a region in southern France ①<u>where</u> the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea. It functions as a natural sponge, ②<u>absorbing</u> and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water ③<u>aid</u> in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place ④<u>to observe</u> more than 400 species of birds.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③aid → aids: 주어가 'Its ability'(3인칭 단수)이므로 동사도 단수형 aids가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ aid → aids: 주어 'Its ability'가 3인칭 단수이므로 -s 필요.
❌ ① where: 관계부사. 장소 선행사(a region) 수식.
❌ ② absorbing: 분사구문. 동시 동작 표현.
❌ ④ to observe: 형용사적 용법의 to부정사.
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: 주어가 단수(ability)이면 동사도 단수(aids).

questions.passage: The Camargue horses are a special breed, ①<u>said</u> to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years ②<u>living</u> in the unique environment of the Camargue and ③<u>adapted</u> to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of ④<u>surviving</u> in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③adapted → adapting: 'have spent ... living and adapting'에서 and 앞뒤로 동명사 병렬이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ adapted → adapting: 'spent + 시간 + V-ing' 구문에서 and 뒤에도 동명사 병렬.
❌ ① said: 과거분사 수동. '~라고 말해지는'. 적절.
❌ ② living: 'spent + 시간 + V-ing' 구문. 적절.
❌ ④ surviving: 'as a result of + V-ing' 전치사 뒤 동명사. 적절.
det.tip: spend + 시간 + V-ing: 병렬 구조에서 and 앞뒤 동일 형태. living and adapting.

questions.passage: What is more, the Everglades is the only place ①<u>where</u> American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, ②<u>whereas</u> alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found ③<u>living</u> together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Unless the Everglades ④<u>is preserving</u>, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④is preserving → is preserved: 에버글레이즈가 보존'되는' 것이므로 수동태가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ is preserving → is preserved: 주어가 보존의 대상이므로 수동태(be + p.p.).
❌ ① where: 관계부사. 'the only place where' 장소 선행사.
❌ ② whereas: 대조 접속사. '반면에'.
❌ ③ living: 'are found living'에서 5형식 보어 현재분사. 적절.
det.tip: 능동 vs 수동: 주어가 행위의 대상이면 수동태. is preserved(보존된다).

questions.passage: The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 습지와 호수가 35%를 차지하므로 새들에게 이상적인(ideal) 장소이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② ideal(이상적인): 35%가 습지/호수이므로 새들에게 최적.
❌ ① isolated(고립된): 관광지이므로 고립과 맞지 않음.
❌ ③ industrial(산업의): 자연 환경 묘사에 부적절.
❌ ④ identical(동일한): 문맥상 무관.
det.tip: ideal(이상적인) = perfect. ideal place for ~ = ~에게 이상적인 장소.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species ①<u>rely</u> on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter. For example, the Florida panther has ②<u>flourished</u> in the Everglades. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③abundant(풍부한) → extinct(멸종된): 1995년에 12마리뿐이었으므로 '풍부한'이 아니라 거의 '멸종된' 상태.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ abundant → extinct: 12마리뿐이면 풍부한 것이 아니라 거의 멸종 상태.
❌ ① rely(의지하다): 먹이, 물, 보호처를 위해 의지하므로 적절.
❌ ② flourished(번성했다): 에버글레이즈에서 잘 살았다는 맥락.
❌ ④ recovered(회복했다): 230마리로 늘었으므로 적절.
det.tip: extinct(멸종된) ↔ abundant(풍부한). 'nearly extinct' = 거의 멸종 상태.

det.korean: 원문: 'Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August' — 7~8월 우기에 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문 그대로. 우포가 7~8월 우기에 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지한다.
det.tip: prevent floods by absorbing water = 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지하다.

questions.stem:

det.korean: 원문: 'more than 400 species of birds' — 400종 이상이므로 '300종 이상'도 참.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 400종 이상이면 당연히 300종 이상도 참.

det.analysis: ✅ F: '아랍어(Arabic)'에서 유래했는데 '라틴어'라고 했으므로 거짓.
det.tip: 세부 사항 변조: Arabic(아랍어)를 Latin(라틴어)으로 바꿔 혼동 유발.

det.analysis:

❌ ① 연약하고 민감: powerful의 반의어.
❌ ② 빠르고 민첩: 언급되지 않은 속성.
❌ ③ 온순하고 차분: 거친 환경 생존과 무관.
det.tip: powerful(힘센) = strong. as a result of ~ing = ~한 결과로.

"에버글레이즈에서 악어와 앨리게이터가 공존하는 이유는 __________이다."

det.korean: 담수와 해수가 만나는 곳에서 함께 살 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 담수와 해수가 만나는 지점: 원문 'where fresh water meets salt water'.
❌ ② 담수에서만: 악어는 해수, 앨리게이터는 담수.
❌ ③ 인공적 관리: 자연적 현상.
❌ ④ 같은 먹이 공유: 먹이 언급 없음.
det.tip: coexist(공존하다). fresh water + salt water = 기수역(brackish water).

✅ ③ 2017년까지 약 230마리 회복: 원문 일치.
❌ ① 'Florida Bay'까지이지 '대서양'이 아님.
❌ ② 1995년에는 '약 12마리'. 230마리는 2017년.
❌ ④ 'biological supermarket(생물학적 슈퍼마켓)'이지 '자연 박물관'이 아님.
det.tip: 숫자/연도 변조 주의: 1995년(12마리) vs 2017년(230마리).

det.analysis:
✅ ② 불일치: 원문은 'cattle herding(목축)'인데 '어업'으로 변조.
❌ ① 일치: 'the largest wetland in Africa'.
❌ ③ 일치: 'sent the military in 61 AD'.
❌ ④ 일치: 'unable to proceed beyond the Sudd'.

questions.passage: Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②remain → remains: 주어 'less than half of the historic Everglades'가 단수이므로 단수 동사 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ② remain → remains: 'less than half'가 주어 — 단수 취급.
❌ ① rise: 'sea levels rise' 복수주어+복수동사 적절.
❌ ③ extraction: 'oil extraction activities'에서 명사 수식 적절.
❌ ④ have disappeared: '64% of wetlands'는 복수이므로 복수 동사 적절.
det.tip: less than half of + 단수명사 → 단수 동사. 'less than half remains(절반도 남지 않는다)'.

questions.passage: Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"에버글레이즈가 보존되지 않으면 수백만 명이 식수 __________을 겪을 것이다."

det.korean: 원문: 'suffer from a shortage of drinking water' — 식수 부족을 겪다.
det.analysis: shortage(부족): 'suffer from a shortage of ~' = ~의 부족을 겪다.
det.tip: shortage(부족) = lack = scarcity. suffer from = ~으로 고통받다.

questions.passage: They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide __________ (number) benefits to both the environment and humans.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 환경과 인간 모두에게 수많은(numerous) 혜택을 제공한다.
det.analysis: number(n. 수) → numerous(adj. 수많은). 'provide ___ benefits'에서 명사를 수식하는 형용사 필요.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 습지가 환경과 인간에게 주는 다양한 혜택

det.korean: 습지가 쓸모없어 보이지만 환경과 인간 모두에게 많은 혜택을 제공하는 독특한 생태계.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 습지의 다양한 혜택: 핵심 — 'provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans'.
❌ ① 역사적 기원: 날짜만 언급.
❌ ② 파괴 원인: 도입부에서는 혜택을 강조.
❌ ③ 관광 산업: 우포는 예시일 뿐.
det.tip: 주제: 반복 핵심어(wetlands, benefits, environment, humans)에 주목.

questions.passage: Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 습지는 중요한 혜택을 제공하지만 현재 다양한 위협에 처해 있다.
기후 변화가 습지 감소의 유일한 원인이다.
습지 보존보다 경제 개발이 더 시급한 문제이다.

det.korean: 습지가 혜택을 제공하지만 기후변화, 도시 개발, 기름 유출 등 위협에 처해 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 혜택 + 위협: 글의 두 핵심.
❌ ② '유일한 원인': 기후변화 외 다양.
❌ ③ '자연적 원인': 인간 활동이 주요 원인.
❌ ④ '경제 개발 시급': 글은 보존을 주장.
det.tip: 요지: 핵심 주장 한 문장 요약. 극단적 표현(유일한) = 대부분 오답.
